Simple explanations

How project management works

Agile

A way of working in small steps, showing progress early and improving from feedback instead of planning everything once.

Scrum

A popular Agile framework. Work is selected from a backlog and completed in short periods called sprints, often lasting one or two weeks.

Jira

A software tool used to record work, assign owners, set priorities, run Scrum boards and report progress. It does not manage the project for you.

Waterfall

A sequential approach: requirements first, then design, build, test and launch. It suits work where requirements are stable.

5CloseApprove, hand over, learn

Complete this 7-day practice

  1. Day 1: Read the charter and explain the project goal aloud.
  2. Day 2: Add three backlog tasks and move one into progress.
  3. Day 3: Review dependencies on the timeline.
  4. Day 4: Add one risk and write a mitigation.
  5. Day 5: Update budget actuals and review variance.
  6. Day 6: Submit and decide a change request.
  7. Day 7: Generate the weekly status report and export the project.

The agreement before work starts

Project scope and charter

Baseline v1.0

Objective

Replace inconsistent manual expense entry with a controlled receipt-to-report workflow that gives the founder timely, categorised expense visibility.

Success measures

  • 90% of receipts captured through one channel
  • Weekly reporting time reduced from hours to minutes
  • Categories applied consistently
  • Oracle itemisation reconciles with the dashboard

Deliverables

  • Receipt submission form
  • Structured Google Sheet
  • Apps Script automation
  • Expense dashboard
  • Quality-check procedure
  • User guide and handover

Out of scope

  • Replacing Oracle
  • Automatic bank payments
  • Changing company finance policy
Why scope matters: it prevents the project from quietly growing beyond the agreed time and budget. Anything new goes through change control.

Sequence and dependencies

Milestones and Gantt timeline

6-week plan

A milestone is a meaningful checkpoint. A dependency means one activity cannot start or finish until another activity happens.

Example dependency: dashboard testing depends on the structured sheet and category rules being ready first.
